extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO staff involved in U.S. patent prosecution, appeals, reexaminations, interferences, and contested Board proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Amendments to 37 CFR Part 1 implementing procedural rules for patent prosecution, appeals, reexaminations, interferences, and contested cases before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (now part 41). Intended to guide filing, timing, service, inventorship corrections, fees, confidentiality, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of new part 41 and related changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide new interference rules in a new part 41 of 37 CFR; provide Subpart A to consolidate general provisions relating to the Board and make them consistent across proceedings; delegate authority from the Director to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge for petitions and limited disqualifications; provide Subpart B rules for ex parte appeals; limit amendments filed on or after filing a brief; change format and content of appeal brief; provide Subpart C rules for inter partes reexamination appeals; provide Subpart D general rules for contested cases (interferences and ownership); provide Subpart E rules specific to patent interferences; clarify when there is an interference-in-fact, how claims correspond to a count, and how benefit of earlier applications is accorded; require applicants adding a claim to provoke an interference to provide additional details; clarify that a two-way unpatentability test is used to determine whether claimed inventions interfere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble states these changes are interpretive rules or rules of agency practice and procedure (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A)) and thus prior notice and comment were not required. The changes relate solely to procedure for filing and prosecuting patent applications, appeals to the Board, and contested cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.1 - Addresses for non-trademark correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences. See § 41.10 of this title. Notices of appeal, appeal briefs, reply briefs, requests for oral hearing, as well as all other correspondence in an application or a patent involved in an appeal to the Board for which an address is not otherwise specified, should be addressed as set out in paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified Board address for all appeal-related correspondence unless another address is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.4 - Nature of correspondence and signature requirements (reference to part 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence in and relating to a particular application or other proceeding in the Office should follow the rules relating to filing, processing, or other proceedings as set out in subparts (including the Board rules in part 41).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See subpart B (national applications), subpart C (international), subpart D (ex parte reexamination), subpart H (inter partes reexamination), and part 41 for Board proceedings; correspondence must comply with the applicable subpart rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.6(d)(9) - Receipt of correspondence in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of correspondence: in contested cases before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences except as the Board may expressly authorize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may set different receipt requirements by express authorization; otherwise contested-case correspondence follows the specified receipt rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.8 - Certificate of mailing or transmission for contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed in contested cases before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences are governed by § 41.106(f) of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates of mailing/transmission for papers in contested cases must meet the requirements set forth in the referenced Board rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.9 - Definitions for Board proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: For definitions in Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences proceedings, see part 41 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms used in Board proceedings should be interpreted according to the definitions supplied in part 41.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.11(e) - Public inspection of interference files
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as prohibited in § 41.6(b), the file of any interference is open to public inspection and copies of the file may be obtained upon payment of the fee therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference files are generally public unless specific exceptions apply under § 41.6(b); copies available for fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.14(e) - Publication or public availability of Director's decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any decision by the Director that would not otherwise be open to public inspection may be published or made available for public inspection if: (1) The Director believes the decision involves an interpretation of patent laws or regulations that would be of precedential value; and (2) The applicant is given notice and an opportunity to object in writing within two months on the ground that the decision discloses a trade secret or other confidential information. Objections must identify deletions or explain why the entire decision must be withheld. The applicant or party will be given at least twenty days to request reconsideration and seek court review before portions are made public over objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director balances precedential value against confidentiality; applicants have a specified objection and reconsideration timeline and must identify confidential material to justify withholding.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.17 - Fees for proceedings before the Board and petition fee list
rubrics_metrics.description: For fees in proceedings before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, see § 41.20 of this title. For filing a petition under one of the listed sections which refers to this paragraph: $130.00. (Lists many sections for which the $130 petition fee applies.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult § 41.20 for Board fees; the $130 petition fee applies to a broad set of petitions enumerated in §1.17(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.36 - Revocation of power of attorney; withdrawal of patent attorney or agent
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney may be revoked at any stage by an applicant or assignee of the entire interest; revocation by fewer than all applicants requires showing sufficient cause and payment of petition fee. A registered patent attorney or agent may withdraw upon application to and approval by the Director; notification to applicant/patent owner is required. Specific rules apply when power is given to practitioners associated with a Customer Number, including limits on deletion when a reply is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation and withdrawal require notice and possibly petition fees; customer-number appointments and in-process deadlines restrict deletion; see § 41.5 for withdrawal during Board proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.48 - Correction of inventorship in nonprovisional application (35 U.S.C. 116)
rubrics_metrics.description: If inventorship is set forth in error without deceptive intention, inventorship may be amended. Amendment requires: (1) request setting forth desired change; (2) statement from each person added/deleted that error occurred without deceptive intention; (3) oath or declaration by actual inventor(s) as required by § 1.63 or permitted by §§ 1.42, 1.43, or 1.47; (4) processing fee set in § 1.17(i); (5) if an assignment was executed, written consent of the assignee. Additional rules govern deletions due to amendment/cancellation of claims and adding inventors for previously unclaimed subject matter. Correction in a contested case must be in the form of a motion under § 41.121(a)(2) and comply with this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different factual scenarios (inventorship error, fewer inventors due to claim changes, adding inventors for newly claimed subject matter) have specified documentary, fee, and consent requirements; contested-case corrections must be presented as specified Board motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.55 - Claim for foreign priority; Office may require earlier filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require the claim for priority and the certified copy of the foreign application be filed earlier than provided when: (i) application becomes involved in an interference (see § 41.202); (ii) necessary to overcome the date of a reference relied upon by the examiner; or (iii) deemed necessary by the examiner. An English translation of a non-English foreign application is not required except when involved in an interference, necessary to overcome a reference, or specifically required by the examiner. If translation is required, it must be filed together with a statement that the translation is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority documentation and translations may be required sooner when interference or prior-art handling demands it; translation requires a certification of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.59 - Expungement of information in application file
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in an application will not be expunged except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section or § 41.7(a) of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expungement is tightly circumscribed; see the cited paragraphs for allowable expungement situations (including Board rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.103(g) - Suspension of action by the Office for statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will suspend action by the Office for the entire pendency of an application if the Office has accepted a request to publish a statutory invention registration in the application, except for purposes relating to patent interference proceedings under part 41, subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of a statutory invention registration request generally suspends Office action, but interference-related actions continue per part 41 subpart D.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.112 - Reconsideration before final action
rubrics_metrics.description: After reply by applicant or patent owner to a non-final action and any comments by an inter partes reexamination requester, the application or patent will be reconsidered and again examined. Applicant (or patent owner and requester in reexam) will be notified if claims are rejected or favorable decisions made. Applicant may reply with or without amendment unless the Office action is made final, an appeal has been taken, or specified final/closing notices have been given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard reconsideration and reply rules apply; examine the specifics for exceptions such as final actions or appeals (see §§ 1.113, 1.116, 41.31, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.113 - Final rejection or action
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination the rejection or other action may be made final. Thereupon applicant's (or patent owner's in ex parte reexam) reply is limited to appeal (§ 41.31) or to amendment as specified in § 1.114 or § 1.116. Petitions may be taken to the Director for objections or requirements not involved in the rejection of any claim (§ 1.181). Reply to a final rejection must comply with § 1.114 or paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rejections limit options to appeal or specified amendments; petitions to the Director available for certain matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.114 - Request for continued examination (RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files a submission and fee set forth in § 1.17(e), the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action and the submission will be entered and considered. If an applicant files an RCE after appeal but prior to a decision on the appeal, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution. An appeal brief or related papers will not be considered a submission under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCEs withdraw finality and reopen prosecution; filing an RCE during an appeal withdraws the appeal. Appeal briefs and brief-related papers are not RCE submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.116 - Amendments and affidavits or other evidence after final action and prior to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final rejection but before or on the same date of filing an appeal: (1) amendments may cancel claims or comply with form requirements; (2) amendments presenting rejected claims in better form for appeal may be admitted; (3) amendments touching merits may be admitted upon showing good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented. Admission or refusal does not relieve appeal condition or save from abandonment. Specific restrictions apply in inter partes reexamination and ex parte reexamination regarding cancellations affecting other pending claims and after right of appeal notice. Affidavits or other evidence may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons. After decision on appeal, amendments, affidavits and other evidence can only be made as provided in §§ 1.198 and 1.981, or to carry into effect a recommendation under § 41.50(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admittance of post-final amendments/evidence requires justification and may be limited by reexamination or appeal status; see referenced sections for special constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.131 - Affidavit or declaration of prior invention and interference suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rejection is based upon a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication of another which claims the same patentable invention as defined in § 41.203(a), an applicant may suggest an interference pursuant to § 41.202(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the examiner relies on a U.S. reference that appears to claim the same invention, suggestion of interference is available under the specified Board rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.136 - Extensions of time (general and sufficient cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the period up to the earlier of the maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply if a petition and fee (§ 1.17(a)) are filed, unless exceptions apply (notification in Office action; reply is a reply brief (§ 41.41); reply is request for oral hearing (§ 41.47(a)); reply to a Board decision (§ 1.304, §41.50, §41.52); application is involved in a contested case (§ 41.101(a)). The date petition and fee are filed determines the period and fee. When paragraph (a) is not available, extension will be granted only for sufficient cause for a reasonable time if requested on or before due date; mere filing of request does not affect extension; no extension beyond maximum statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions via petition+fee are available subject to listed exceptions; otherwise only sufficient-cause extensions on timely request; statutory maximum cannot be exceeded; cross-references to other extension provisions for appeals and reexaminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.181 - Petition to the Director (invoke supervisory authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions may be filed to invoke the supervisory authority of the Director in appropriate circumstances. For petitions involving action of the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, see § 41.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use petition procedures to seek Director intervention; Board-specific petitions follow part 41 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.191 - Appeal to Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences under 35 U.S.C. 134(a) and (b) are conducted according to part 41 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All appeals under the cited statutes follow the Board procedural rules in part 41.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.197 - Return of jurisdiction from the Board; termination of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over an application or patent under ex parte reexamination passes to the examiner after a decision by the Board upon transmittal of the file, subject to appellant’s right of appeal or other review, for further action as required to carry into effect the Board decision. Proceedings on an application are considered terminated by dismissal of an appeal or failure to timely file appeal to the court or a civil action except where claims stand allowed or further action by the examiner is required. The date of termination is the date of dismissal or expiration of time for appeal; if appeal/civil action filed, termination is when such proceedings terminate (e.g., issuance of mandate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal triggers examiner jurisdiction for carrying out Board decisions; termination definitions tie to appeal filing dates and dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.198 - Reopening after a final decision of the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision by the Board on appeal has become final for judicial review, prosecution before the primary examiner will not be reopened or reconsidered except under § 1.114 or § 41.50 and only with written authority of the Director, and then only for consideration of matters not already adjudicated, sufficient cause being shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening is tightly limited: generally only via RCE or specified Board procedures and only with Director authorization for non-adjudicated matters with sufficient cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.248(c) - Service of papers in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: See § 41.105(f) of this title for service of papers in contested cases before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service requirements for contested-case papers are governed by the referenced Board rule; follow § 41.105(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.292 - Public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition for institution of public use proceedings, supported by affidavits or declarations, is found on reference to the examiner to make a prima facie showing that an invention had been in public use or on sale more than one year before filing, a hearing may be held before the Director to determine whether to institute proceedings. If instituted, the Director may designate an official to conduct the public use proceeding and set times for testimony, to be taken as provided by part 41, subpart D. The petitioner will be heard in the proceedings but after decision will not be heard further in the prosecution of the application. A petition for institution of public use proceedings shall not be filed by a party to an interference as to an application involved in the interference; public use and on-sale issues in an interference shall be raised by a motion under § 41.121(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-use proceedings require a prima facie showing; hearing procedures follow Board subpart D; parties to an interference must raise such issues via Board motion, not by separate public-use petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.295 - Review of decision refusing to publish a statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any requester dissatisfied with a decision finally rejecting claims pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 112 may obtain review by filing an appeal to the Board pursuant to § 41.31. If the decision rejecting claims under 35 U.S.C. 112 is reversed, the request for a statutory invention registration will be approved and the registration published if all other provisions of § 1.293 and this section are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal to the Board is the remedy for final 112 rejections in this context; reversal can lead to approval/publication subject to meeting other statutory/regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.302 - Notice of appeal service in interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: In interferences, the notice [of appeal] must be served as provided in § 41.106(f) of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service of notice of appeal for interference-involved matters must follow Board service rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.303(c) - Civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145/146/306; notice of election service
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of election under 35 U.S.C. 141 to have proceedings on review conducted as provided in 35 U.S.C. 146 must be filed with the Office of the Solicitor and served as provided in § 41.106(f) of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing and service of election notices for civil action procedure must follow the specified filing location and Board service format.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.304 - Time for appeal or civil action (governs appeal timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for filing the notice of appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (§ 1.302) or for commencing a civil action (§ 1.303) is governed by § 1.304; (text continues beyond chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section sets the deadlines for filing appeals to the Federal Circuit or commencing civil actions; consult the full § 1.304 text for specific time periods and interplay with Board decisions.
